exercise.name: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
aliases: Lying dumbbell external rotation (arm out to the side)

reference.title: Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation
reference.listing: Page not read (gymvisual.com is blocked by the proxy); movement taken from the exercise name and standard coaching practice.
reference.note: Reference used only to identify the movement. No GymVisual media is stored here; this rig, model and animation are original.

breathing.pattern: Breathe out as the forearm rotates up to vertical, breathe in as it lowers toward the feet.
breathing.cadence: About 2 s up, short pause, about 2.5 s down

prescription.effort: Stop 2-3 reps short of failure (RIR 2-3); no pain
prescription.progression: Add reps, then a slightly heavier dumbbell

cues.text: Lie on your back, knees bent, feet flat. Right upper arm out to the side on the floor, a little below shoulder height, elbow bent 90 degrees; the forearm points toward the feet with the dumbbell just off the floor, palm down.
Breathe out and turn the forearm up about the elbow until it points at the ceiling; the upper arm stays on the floor.
Forearm vertical; elbow still at 90 degrees.
Breathe in and lower slowly back toward the feet.
Pause just off the floor and repeat. Then switch sides.

mistakes.mistake: Upper arm lifting off the floor
mistakes.fix: Keep the elbow and upper arm heavy on the floor.
Hold the elbow at 90 degrees the whole time.
Keep the ribs down and the back flat.
Take two to three seconds down.

kinematics.norm: From the forearm pointing toward the feet (internal rotation) up to vertical, rotating against gravity (clinical opinion); external rotation at 90 degrees of abduction loads the infraspinatus and teres minor (Reinold 2004)
Upper arm out to the side, about 70-90 degrees, resting on the floor (clinical opinion)

sources.title: GymVisual #25915, Dumbbell Lying External Shoulder Rotation, video (movement reference only; page not read)

Reinold, Wilk, Fleisig, Zheng, Barrentine, Chmielewski, Cody, Jameson and Andrews 2004, electromyographic analysis of the rotator cuff and deltoid musculature during common shoulder external rotation exercises (J Orthop Sports Phys Ther 34(7):385-394)

cautions: Stop if sharp pain, a pinching feeling in the front or top of the shoulder, numbness or tingling occurs.
The dumbbell load is user-chosen: pick a weight you can control for every rep with good form.
Muscle glow colours and activation curves are illustrative, not measured EMG.
Rotator cuff work: use a light dumbbell and a slow, pain-free range.
modify: Shoulder discomfort: lower the upper arm toward the side (less abduction) and shorten the range.

muscleNotes.infraspinatus_r: Prime mover (with teres minor): lifts the forearm from pointing at the feet to vertical (external rotation).
muscleNotes.post_deltoid_r: Assists external rotation with the arm abducted.
muscleNotes.rhomboids_midtrap_r: Keep the shoulder blade on the floor.

phases.label: Arm out, forearm toward the feet

guides.label: Forearm turns up about the elbow
